title: Policy Engine: Targeted Batching & Caching Controls by Customer Segment and Route
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Build a policy engine that applies batching and caching recommendations at per-customer and per-route granularity. The engine should support segmentation (by customer tier, traffic fingerprint, and SLA), allowlists/denylists for routes and customers, and tier-based controls (e.g., premium vs. free). It must automate safe config application with dry-run, canary, and simulated billing modes and expose automatic rollback hooks tied to SLO/cost/quality thresholds.
background: We currently apply global batching/caching heuristics that sometimes harm tail latency or deliver suboptimal cost savings for high-SLA customers. Customers have asked for finer-grained controls and for the platform to suggest safe optimizations automatically. This ticket scopes a first-pass policy engine and the guardrails needed to apply changes safely across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
proposal:
- Introduce a policy model that maps segmentation keys (customer_id, plan_tier, route_id, path_regex, request_metadata) to optimization profiles (batch_size_target, kv_cache_policy, prefix_cache_enabled, quantization_suggestion).
- Support allowlist/denylist rules for both customers and routes; denylisted routes are excluded from any aggressive batching/caching to preserve latency and quality.
- Tier controls: default profiles per plan_tier with override precedence: route_allowlist > customer_override > tier_default > global_fallback.
- Recommendation engine: periodic analysis job that samples token distributions, latency percentiles, and cost-per-1k-tokens per route/customer and proposes config diffs ranked by estimated monthly savings and risk score.
- Safe apply: dry-run (estimate only), canary (small % of traffic or specific customer subset), and staged rollout with automated rollback triggers (latency spike, quality regression, error rate increase, cost anomaly).
implementation_notes:
- Data inputs: per-route request histogram (seq_len), per-customer token counts, response latency p50/p95/p99, error_rate, output_quality_metrics from eval harness.
- Storage: store policy snapshots in config-store with versioning and rollback token.
- Engine: stateless controller that generates candidate config diffs; config appliers run via rollout service.
- Integration points: runtime routing layer (to apply batching targets), KV cache manager (to enable prefix caching), console (UI for rules), optimize service (to show recommendations), billing estimator (to calculate projected savings).
- Safety: require a safe-apply feature flag and a security review for any automatic apply path that affects premium customers.
acceptance_criteria:
- Policy engine can create, list, and version policies scoped to customer_id and route_id.
- System can run a recommendation pass and output at least 3 savings-ranked suggestions for the staging cluster.
- Dry-run mode produces estimated token cost delta and projected latency impact without changing runtime behavior.
- Canary rollout can be targeted by customer IDs or by route regex and limited to a traffic percent.
- Automatic rollback triggers fire and revert canary changes when p95 latency increases > 25% or error_rate increases > 0.5% relative to baseline.
- Console shows per-policy expected savings and risk score.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for policy precedence logic and config serialization.
- Integration tests: simulated traffic with variable seq_len distributions to validate batching thresholds affect cost/latency as expected.
- End-to-end: deploy to staging, run recommendation job against one high-traffic route, perform dry-run, execute canary for 5% traffic, assert no regression, then escalate to 50% and assert metrics match estimates within 10%.
- Add chaos test where rollout is forced to trigger rollback and verify snapshot restore and alerting.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge controller and console PRs behind feature flag. 2) Run recommendation job in read-only (dry-run) mode for 2 weeks to gather baseline alerts and validate savings estimates. 3) Onboard a single internal customer segment (low-risk internal accounts) and route set as canary. 4) Promote to broader cohorts (non-SLA-sensitive customers) once canary passes for 48h. 5) Expose UI and allowlist UX for customer-success teams to opt-in. 6) Gradually enable automated apply for selected low-risk tiers only.
rollback_plan:
- All applied policy changes are stored as versioned snapshots with a rollback token.
- Rollback triggers: automated alarms for p95 latency delta > 25%, error_rate delta > 0.5%, quality regression score drop > 3 points, or unexpected cost increase above projected.
- Rollback actions: immediate revert to previous snapshot, notify on-call and affected customers, and open automated postmortem stub with request/response logs for the canary window.
